entities.summary: Juan Bautista Diamante, minor Spanish dramatist of the school of Calderón, was the son of a Portuguese mother and a Sicilian merchant of Greek parentage who came to Madrid some time before 1631. He began writing for the stage in the early 1650s, gained favour at the courts of Philip IV and Charles II, and became a knight of St. John in 1660. It has been suggested  that Juan Bautista may have been of Jewish stock, and that the Diamante family, including the playwright's half-brothers Pablo and Francisco Diamante who also achieved success in their different spheres, falsified public records of marriage, baptism, etc.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Juan Bautista Diamante's success in the Spanish court influenced his half-brothers' careers and may have contributed to the falsification of public records by the Diamante family, potentially affecting historical records of Jewish identity in Spain.
